report.summary: Analyzed chunk 2 of cycles.py: functions self_loops, nontrivial_components, component_edges, cycle_report with docstrings and code.
risks: self_loops | low | Uses 'edges[src] or ()' which may iterate over a string if edges[src] is a string, not an iterable of strings. Assumes edges values are iterables. | Check that edges values are always iterables (e.g., list, tuple, set) and not strings.

nontrivial_components | medium | Relies on strongly_connected_components (imported) which is not defined in this chunk. If that function is missing or incorrect, results are wrong. | Ensure strongly_connected_components is defined and correct.

cycle_report | medium | Uses index.get('import_edges') which may be None or missing; code handles with 'or {}'. But if import_edges is present but not a Mapping, errors may occur. | Ensure import_edges is a Mapping[str, Iterable[str]] or handle type mismatch.
cycle_report | low | Computes n_modules by union of keys and all values; this may double-count if a module appears as both key and value. | Verify that n_modules count is as intended.
cycle_report | low | n_edges uses sum(len(list(...))) which is inefficient; also assumes edges[s] is iterable. | Consider using sum(1 for s in edges for d in edges[s] or ()).

handoff.purpose: Defines functions for self-loops, nontrivial components, component edges, and cycle report generation.

symbols.name: self_loops
symbols.note: Returns tuple of modules that import themselves (self-loop edges).

symbols.name: nontrivial_components
symbols.note: Returns SCCs that are cycles: size >1 or self-loop.

symbols.name: component_edges
symbols.note: Returns sorted tuple of induced edges within a component.

symbols.name: cycle_report
symbols.note: Returns dict with cycle structure of an index's import edges.

claims.text: Modules that import themselves. Reported separately because a self-loop is a one-node SCC and would otherwise be indistinguishable from an ordinary leaf -- and a module importing itself is a real finding, not a trivial component.
claims.why: The function returns src where src in edges[src]; this identifies self-loops. The claim about indistinguishability from leaf is uncheckable but the behavior matches.

claims.text: SCCs that are actually cycles: more than one member, or a self-loop.
claims.why: The function filters components: len(c)>1 or (len(c)==1 and c[0] in loops). This matches the claim.

claims.text: The edges induced by ``component`` -- i.e. the ones a cut must consider. This is the input to any feedback-arc question. Sorted, so a proposed cut can be quoted in a review and re-derived later.
claims.why: Function returns sorted tuple of edges where both src and dst are in component. Sorting ensures reproducibility.

claims.text: The cycle structure of a built index, as a receipt-shaped dict. Reads ``index["import_edges"]``, which is the layer that ALREADY includes function-body imports -- ``parse._import_records`` walks every node with ``ast.walk`` and records no scope. That is why this is worth computing at all: a cycle detector fed only top-level imports would have reported this repo as acyclic, which is true at import time and false as a change-propagation question. 37% of internal edges live inside function bodies.
claims.why: Claims about parse._import_records, ast.walk, and 37% statistic refer to code outside this chunk; cannot verify.

claims.text: Passing ``index`` avoids a rebuild; omitting it uses the process-wide cache.
claims.why: Code shows if index is None, calls cached_index; but cached_index is imported from .index and not defined here. The behavior depends on that import.

observations.what: self_loops uses 'edges[src] or ()' which may not work correctly if edges[src] is an empty string; it would treat empty string as falsy and return (). Also if edges[src] is a string, iterating over it yields characters.
nontrivial_components depends on strongly_connected_components which is not defined in this chunk; it must be imported or defined elsewhere.
component_edges uses set(out) to deduplicate; but out is built as list of tuples of strings, so set works. Sorting ensures consistent order.

cycle_report computes n_modules as len({*edges, *(d for s in edges for d in edges[s] or ())}). This creates a set of all keys and all values; but if edges[s] is a string, iterating yields characters, corrupting the module set.
cycle_report computes n_edges as sum(len(list(edges[s] or ())) for s in edges). This is inefficient and assumes edges[s] is iterable; if it's a string, len(list(...)) gives character count.
cycle_report accesses components[0] without checking if components is non-empty; if empty, IndexError.
